Senses.Explanation: Literally, to have no measure or placement available. The phrase occurs 936 times in 220 allowlisted texts and most characteristically records the moment after a question, silence, shout, blow, or other public exchange when a participant has no response. Wenxi remains at a loss after the master answers his question about himself with silence; an emperor is at a loss when National Teacher Nanyang Huizhong sits silent after requesting a seamless-stupa design; and in Linji's record a monk is at a loss after Linji laughs and is then struck. Later records also use it retrospectively: the later Baoshou is at a loss when asked for the original face before his parents were born. The expression names the reported failure to answer; the records do not make the word itself a diagnosis of an inward state.
Senses.Note: No separate Zen-technical object emerged. Ordinary inability to know what to do is bent into a recurrent public-interview report, commonly placed directly before the master's next action. Formula searches produced no corpus definition of the word; the deployment, not an imported psychological gloss, fixes the entry.
